sheet-1-1.description: The main map of Sheet 1 of the July 1920 Sanborn atlas of Bridgeport, Logan Township, Gloucester County, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It covers the eastern end of the village: both sides of Main Street from the junction with Swedesboro (today Church Street) eastward to the last lots of the built-up street, and the short stretch of Mechanic Street west of Swedesboro, with Swedesboro itself running south-south-east towards the railroad, which lies about 80 feet beyond the bottom of the sheet. The north side of Main is a single row of deep lots, numbered 103 to 120, with frame dwellings, auto sheds and wagon sheds, the Peerless Garage with an auto repair shop at the west end, and Logan Hall, a three-storey frame hall. A heavy line along the rear of these lots marks the limit of the survey, with the ground beyond lettered vacant. South of Main, east of Swedesboro, are frame dwellings on lots 127 to 140, some stuccoed, with sheds and coops behind; west of Swedesboro are St. Paul's M. E. Church with its tower, dwellings on Mechanic Street and the eastern ends of the blocks continued on Sheet 2. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches run under Main, Mechanic and Swedesboro, with several hydrants. Most buildings are frame dwellings of one and a half to two and a half storeys. The top of the sheet carries the title cartouche, a small key map of the village, a locator map of New Jersey, the street and specials index and notes on the water supply and fire department; these are outside this part. A separate inset at the lower right, part 2, shows Main Street further east.
notes: Swedesboro is today Church Street; Mechanic Street ends at it on the sheet but continues east today.
Placed by a helmert transformation from two hand-picked junctions on Church Street; low confidence in rotation.
Main Street lot numbers 103 to 140 on this part continue the numbering of Sheet 2.

Map, 50 ft. Title sheet with key map (to 400-ish scale, cut out of mask), index and water/fire notes at top; part 1: Main Street east of old Swedesboro (now Church Street), Swedesboro and Mechanic; part 2: inset at lower right bounded by heavy lines, Main Street lots 145-147 further east (vegetable packing), no cross street.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Main Street lots 145-147 east of part 1 (vegetable packing shed) (no street junction or feature shared with another sheet; only Main Street drawn, position along it unknown; needs a dated cross street or building identified on the ground along East Main Street).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 of the July 1920 Sanborn atlas of Bridgeport, Logan Township, Gloucester County, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It shows the centre of the village between an alley on the west (today Springer Road) and the eastern lots carried on Sheet 1: both sides of Main Street, the blocks between Main and Mechanic Street, and south of Mechanic the blocks along Railroad Avenue and Cooper (today Law Street) down to Station Avenue and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, Penns Grove Branch, lettered P. R. R. The north side of Main is a row of deep lots with frame dwellings, the Bridgeport Fire Company house with hose carts, a general store, a hall and stables and sheds behind. Between Main and Mechanic are dwellings, a blacksmith shop, a building with the post office, cigars and a club and hall above at the alley corner, and the public school on the east block. South of Mechanic are dwellings along Railroad Avenue, carpenter shops and coops, and east of Cooper an open block with a baseball park, bleacher seats and a stand. Along the railroad are the Bridgeport station with the Keystone Express office, a freight platform, oil houses, a 35,000 gallon water tank on a steel support and a section house. The ground north of Main and south of the railroad is lettered vacant. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches with hydrants run under the streets. Most buildings are frame, one to two and a half storeys. A compass rose stands in the baseball park and the scale bar at the bottom right.
notes: Cooper is today Law Street; Station Avenue is Station Road; the alley at the west edge is Springer Road.
The alley is drawn 24 ft wide against about 50 ft in today's parcels; its two junctions are flagged narrow but sit within 1.1 m of the fit.
Logan Lane, which crosses Mechanic Street and Station Road at the east of the sheet today, is not drawn.

Map, 50 ft. Main, Mechanic, Alley (now Springer Road), Railroad Av, Cooper (now Law Street), Station Av (now Station Road), the West Jersey & Seashore R.R. (Penns Grove Br.); public school, fire company, baseball park.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 of the July 1920 Sanborn atlas of Bridgeport, Logan Township, Gloucester County, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It covers the western end of the village from Raccoon Creek, shown with its bank coloured blue, east to the alleys continued on Sheet 2. Main Street enters across a bridge over the creek and is crossed near the bank by a road running north and south, the north arm with a hotel, hardware store and coal yard at the corner, the south arm running down past the creek bank to the railroad. Further east an alley runs north from Main (today Sheets Road) and another runs south to Mechanic Street (today Springer Road); Railroad, today Railroad Avenue, runs south from Mechanic at the right edge. North of Main are deep lots with dwellings, a barber shop, an ice cream and grocery store, wagon sheds, lumber sheds and a vacant shed. Between Main and Mechanic are stores and dwellings, a grocery, kerosene and gasoline tanks buried at the kerb, a meat shop and stables; a stone dwelling is coloured blue. South of Mechanic are dwellings, hen houses and a large open block with a saw mill and a coal and wood shed, and along Railroad a row of dwellings and a stock room. At the bottom the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, Penns Grove Branch, crosses the sheet, with the Bridgeport Water Company pumping station and its 55,000 gallon tank on steel supports in the corner. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches with hydrants run under the streets. The compass rose and scale bar stand in the creek at the lower left.
notes: The road crossing Main Street by the creek is today South Bridgeport Road south of Main and Island Road north of it; the modern junctions with Main are offset from the drawn crossing, so the Main Street / South Bridgeport Road junction was excluded.
The alley north of Main is Sheets Road and the alley south of Main is Springer Road; Railroad is Railroad Avenue.
Main Street / Sheets Road was hand-picked (the 20 ft alley is too narrow for the detector).
A bridge carries Main Street over Raccoon Creek at the left edge.

Map, 50 ft. West end at Raccoon Creek: Main, Mechanic, Road (now South Bridgeport Road south of Main), Alley north of Main (now Sheets Road), Alley south of Main (now Springer Road), Railroad (Avenue); hotel, coal yard, lumber sheds, Bridgeport Water Co. pumping station.
